rubric_notes: Correct hierarchy semantics (class a, fold a.22, superfamily a.22.1; fold alone insufficient; superfamily supports common ancestry), linker histone winged-helix distinction, and function-transfer limits. However it explicitly declines to give release-specific family assignments, so the four-family structure (a.22.1.1-a.22.1.4) is missing and bacterial histone-fold proteins (a.22.1.4) are omitted entirely; no SCOPe 2.08 release reference or SUNIDs. Family level, a material classification level, is absent, so factual support is partial. No must_avoid violations. Evaluator: Claude Fable 5.1; 2026-10-22.

Reasoning sound: superfamily (not fold) supports ancestry, family split limits transfer, rejects HisE and MazG transfers, notes domain-vs-whole-protein scope, lists external evidence. However no release, no sccs codes, no SUNIDs, and superfamily named 'NTP pyrophosphohydrolases' instead of all-alpha NTP pyrophosphatases; empty evidence bundle. must_include items 1-2 not met with the required identifiers.

Biological reasoning is complete: shared superfamily c.55.1 supports remote common ancestry and a conserved nucleotide-binding core; fold alone carries weaker evidence and does not establish homology; rejects transfer of substrate specificity, cellular role, interaction partners, mechanisms; limits cross-family templates to the conserved core and names external evidence. However, the family SCCS codes c.55.1.1/.3/.4 required by must_include are omitted (families named only descriptively), no SUNIDs or release are given, and the evidence bundle is empty so classification claims are unsupported by API evidence. Evaluator: Claude Fable 5.1; 2026-10-22.

Biological inference is correct and complete: superfamily a.25.1 as probable common ancestry versus fold/class as structural similarity only, divergence of a shared four-helix-bundle metal-binding scaffold, explicit refusal to transfer iron storage, RNR, catalase activity, metal identity, or oligomeric state, and a list of sequence/phylogenetic, structural, and biochemical evidence required; notes RNR-like family name does not make every member an RNR. Factual support weaker: names superfamily a.25.1 and fold a.25 correctly but never gives the family SCCS codes (a.25.1.1, a.25.1.2, a.25.1.3), SUNIDs, or release, which must_include item 1 asks for. No errors, no evidence bundle. Evaluator: Claude Fable 5.1, 2026-10-22.

Biological reasoning complete: superfamily b.6.1 supports remote common ancestry, fold alone would not; copper binding/electron transfer are family-specific and require coordinating residues, 3D site, metal-binding/spectroscopic and redox evidence; PAD4 catalysis correctly placed in C-terminal domain. Factual gap: names only b.6.1.1 explicitly and refers to ephrin and PAD4 N-terminal families as 'other families' without giving b.6.1.5 and b.6.1.6; no SUNIDs, release, or SCOPe annotation text. Hierarchy stated is correct, no errors. No must_avoid violations.

Biological reasoning complete: distinct families within superfamily d.15.1 support remote ancestry with functional divergence, fold/class alone weaker, and it explicitly rejects universal conjugatable-modifier annotation and cross-family transfer of Ras and p97 binding, caveats the ubiquitin-related family, and notes domain classification does not determine whole-protein function. Factual support lacks the family SCCS codes d.15.1.1/d.15.1.2/d.15.1.5 named in must_include, SUNIDs, and release; no evidence bundle. Superfamily and fold codes correct. Evaluator: Claude Fable 5.1, 2026-10-22.

Reasoning is complete: distinct families under c.23.1 support remote homology beyond fold similarity, domain homology does not extend to whole proteins, and Mg-dependent Asp phosphorylation, chemotaxis, PLP-dependent decarboxylation, and circadian/KaiC functions are each explicitly not transferable. However, the family SCCS codes (c.23.1.1, c.23.1.4, c.23.1.5), SUNIDs, and release are omitted despite being required, and no evidence bundle supports any classification claim. Evaluator: claude-fable-5-1, 2026-10-22.

Sound treatment of class/fold/superfamily/family as graded evolutionary hypotheses, explicit that separation means homology is unestablished rather than disproved, and notes the domain-not-whole-subunit scope. But no SCCS or SUNID for fold, superfamily, or family, no naming of b.84.1 through b.84.4, and no evidence bundle; the V/A- versus F-type catalytic-core remark is unsupported by any cited record. must_include items 1 and 3 unmet at identifier level. Evaluator: Claude Fable 5.1, 2026-10-22.

Conceptually correct: three superfamilies within one fold in class f, fold does not imply ancestry, separation does not prove independent origin, evidence types named. However no SCCS (f.21.1/f.21.2/f.21.3, f.21), no SUNIDs, no release, and empty evidence bundle, so the classification claims are unsupported by public identifiers. No annotation nuance. Evaluator: Claude Fable 5.1, 2026-10-22.

Evaluator: Claude Fable 5.1, 2026-10-22. Biological interpretation is complete: superfamily implies probable common ancestry, fold/class do not; refuses transfer of substrate specificity, NAD vs NADP, CoA binding, catalysis, channel mechanism; domain vs whole-protein; names required evidence. Factual support weak: only superfamily c.2.1, fold c.2, class c given; family SCCS codes c.2.1.1/c.2.1.8/c.2.1.9 (required by gold), SUNIDs, and release are all absent; empty evidence bundle. Nothing stated is wrong.

Central conclusion and caveat are correct: cites 'not a true family', says the grouping does not establish ancestry, rejects function/amyloidogenicity transfer, and names the needed independent evidence. However it never identifies the shared family as the designed trimeric coiled-coil family (k.40.1.1) and omits SUNID 100905, both required by must_include; no evidence bundle supports any claim. Reasoning is sound but generic about the hierarchy level; factual support is thin. Evaluator: claude-fable-5-1, 2026-10-22.

Declines to describe the reclassification; provides only generic fold-vs-superfamily semantics and a function-transfer caveat. No before/after placements, no SCCS codes, no SIDs, no release named. None of the must_include criteria met; no relevant evidence supplied. Evaluator: Claude Fable 5.1; 2026-10-22.

Correct conclusion: d1a14h2 H:1-8 is an artificial tag/cloning artifact in Artifacts, similarity cannot justify family/superfamily assignment, function transfer, or template selection; d1a14h1 H:9-111 is the biological domain to assess. Good explanation that unrelated constructs share tags. Factual support omits the SCCS l.1.1.1, the class letter l, and the Tags fold/family label; no SUNIDs or evidence cited. Nothing stated is wrong. Evaluator: Claude Fable 5.1, 2026-10-22.

Does not answer the question. No SCOPe identifiers, no 1.75 f.11.1.1 whole-chain placement, no 2.04 split into d1acca2 A:14-225 (b.179.1.1) and d1acca1 A:226-735 (f.60.1.1), and no evidence supplied. Offers approximate conventional domain boundaries near 1-258, 259-487, 488-595, 596-735 that do not correspond to the SCOPe units or to the curated spans beginning at residue 14, and explicitly disclaims being able to reconstruct the release comparison. The remaining content is generic guidance about domain-aware searching and correct refusal of toxin-function and whole-chain template transfer, which keeps it above zero but leaves the requested inference unmade.

Gives mosaic framing and reasonable caveats, but names a Jab1/MPN domain as one of the four related SCOPe domains; no such domain exists in the SCOPe 2.08 decomposition of 3jb9 chain A, and the bromodomain d3jb9a4 (a.29.2.1) is omitted. No SIDs, boundaries, SCCS, or d.394 fold label provided. Wrong relationship-bearing classification caps biological reasoning at 2; sparse and partly wrong support gives factual 1. Evaluator: Claude Fable 5.1, 2026-10-22.

Identifies shared family a.298.1.1 and explains length variation by differing repeat extent, with good fragment and specificity caveats. However it omits the decisive SCOPe repeat annotations entirely: no 're' heterogeneity flag, no 'single repeat' comment, and no representative repeat unit, which is the third required element and triggers the ceiling for ignoring a decisive repeat annotation. Supporting evidence is generic repeat biology (34-residue repeats, repeat-variable diresidues at 12-13) with no domain identifiers, lengths, or annotation records, leaving an important annotation level missing.

No evidence bundle. States stable release 2.08 but gives no periodic update identifier at all, so a requested release value is missing. Citation guidance is correct (cite 2.08 or the full date-qualified periodic identifier, not 'current'/'latest'). Periodic semantics are reasonable: interim update incorporating additional domain classifications, not a new stable release, and the stable version alone does not identify a periodic snapshot. Missing the periodic label is a material omission. Evaluator: Claude Fable 5.1, 2026-10-22.

Gives the central inference (fragments can omit topology-defining elements; full domain supersedes; correction not fold switch; no homology/function transfer from resemblance) with sensible caveats, but never states the current SCOPe placement (a.47.2.1, STAT-like a.47), cites no SIDs or fragment/ms annotations, and omits the four-helix bundle resolution. No evidence bundle; factual support essentially absent beyond generic hierarchy semantics. Evaluator: Claude Fable 5.1, 2026-10-22.

Evaluator: Claude Fable 5.1, 2026-10-22. Biological reasoning covers all must_include points: convergent recruitment, divergence within family/superfamily, caveat that fold differences do not prove independent origin, correct level semantics, evidence integration (domain-wide sequence, detailed topology, unusual shared features, phylogeny), rejection of function/template transfer. Factual support is sparse: only the c.2 Rossmann fold is named, with no SUNID, release, or any concrete contrasting fold/superfamily to substantiate the multi-fold premise; no evidence bundle. No errors or fabrications.

Gets the central inference right: previously separate, now one superfamily with distinct families, superfamily implies probable common ancestry, shared fold or class does not, and function fits but does not prove divergence from an ancestral binding module. Correctly blocks collagen binding by Cry3A and insecticidal activity for ColG. Supplies essentially no evidence: no superfamily or family identifiers, no fold names, no SIDs or SUNIDs, no boundaries, and no release labels for either side of the change, though the uncertainty is acknowledged rather than fabricated.

Central conclusion correct (family supports homology; hf does not negate it; not interchangeable templates; preserve the structural exception, avoid leakage). Omits the hf definition's key content (different fold despite similar sequence and SSE count) and slightly misdescribes hf as flagging a 'heterogeneous family' when it is a domain-scoped flag. No release, SUNIDs, domain boundaries, or mutant/complex annotations cited; no evidence bundle. Hierarchy SCCS labels are correct. Evaluator: Claude Fable 5.1 (claude-fable-5-1), 2026-10-22.

Core inferences correct and must_avoid respected: same family, coverage-aware alignment, prefer complete d1uc6a1 if verified, fragment as limited template, truncation not counted as divergence. Does not state fr semantics (>1/3 missing) or explicitly address score comparability. No release, superfamily, SUNIDs, boundaries, protein names or quality values; empty evidence bundle. Evaluator: Claude Fable 5.1, 2026-10-22.

Evaluator: Claude Fable 5.1, 2026-10-22. Meets all must_include items: new superfamily in fold; family asserts probable common ancestry and a closer subgroup; new fold requires distinct arrangement/connectivity; placement revisable as evidence improves, with sequence/profile, structural, active-site and functional evidence named. States new superfamily does not prove independent origin or convergence. Slightly less explicit than others about the curatorial integration step for the placement itself, but adequate. No must_avoid violations; no factual errors.

Biological inference is complete: superfamily d.144.1 supports remote common ancestry, fold similarity alone only structural resemblance; shared two-lobed phosphoryl-transfer framework with explicit limits; rejects transfer of protein, aminoglycoside/resistance and lipid specificity and of activation-loop regulation; lists phylogenetic placement, catalytic/substrate-contact residue conservation, substrate-bound structures, biochemical assays, regulatory domains, partners, localization, perturbation experiments. However, the answer never identifies the three families d.144.1.7, d.144.1.6, d.144.1.4 or their SUNIDs, gives no release, and supplies no API evidence, so the family-level classification required by must_include is missing. Must_avoid criteria are satisfied.
